title: Debug Logging and Diagnostic Data knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Debug Logging and Diagnostic Data?
options: Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
Debug logging and diagnostic artifacts can reveal runner behavior but should be enabled deliberately and sanitized to avoid leaking environment data.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
questions.answer_key: Debug logging and diagnostic artifacts can reveal runner behavior but should be enabled deliberately and sanitized to avoid leaking environment data.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of debug logging and diagnostic data: Debug logging and diagnostic artifacts can reveal runner behavior but should be enabled deliberately and sanitized to avoid leaking environment data. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.answer_key: Make the workflow contract explicit: identify the event, job runner, inputs, command/action, output, and failure signal. Keep steps small and review the permissions and source of every action.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to debug logging and diagnostic data?
options: Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: Debug logging and diagnostic artifacts can reveal runner behavior but should be enabled deliberately and sanitized to avoid leaking environment data. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
